title: Digital images and pixels
examples: How big is a pixel really?
What does resolution mean for a photo?
Why do some images look fuzzy?

explain.say: Today we are learning about digital images and pixels.

draw.text: Pixels: The building blocks of images

explain.say: A pixel is just a tiny square dot on a screen.
Resolution tells us how many pixels fit in an image.
RGB stands for Red, Green, and Blue light colours.
Compression shrinks a file by removing extra colour information.
When you zoom in too much, the pixels become visible squares.

faq.q: What is the difference between a pixel and a dot?
faq.a: A pixel is the technical name for the tiny dot of colour on a screen. It is the smallest unit of digital colour.
asks: What is the smallest part of a digital image?
Are pixels just little coloured dots?

faq.q: Why is high resolution better than low resolution?
faq.a: High resolution means there are many more pixels packed into the same space. This keeps the image looking sharper and clearer.
asks: Does more resolution mean a better photo?
What is the benefit of high pixel count?

faq.q: What does RGB mean when talking about colours?
faq.a: It refers to the three primary colours of light: Red, Green, and Blue. Mixing these three colours in different amounts creates all other colours.
asks: What are the primary colours of light?

faq.q: Is compression always bad for an image?
faq.a: Compression makes files smaller, which is good for sending, but too much compression can lose important visual detail.
asks: Can I make a file smaller without losing quality?

faq.q: If I use a low-resolution photo, what happens?
faq.a: The photo will look blocky or fuzzy when you view it large. This is because the original image did not have enough pixels to cover the area.
asks: What happens if I print a small photo big?
Will a low-res image look bad?

facts: Pixels are the basic building blocks of all digital images.
Resolution is measured by the total number of pixels, like megapixels.
The RGB model uses Red, Green, and Blue light to create colour.
Compression reduces file size by discarding some image data.

quiz.say: If an image has 4000 by 3000 pixels, what is its resolution?
quiz.why: The resolution is simply the width multiplied by the height in pixels.

wrong.0: Dividing them gives a ratio, not the standard resolution format.
wrong.2: This is the total number of pixels, not the resolution measurement.
wrong.3: Adding them gives a total count, but resolution needs both measurements.

quiz.say: Which combination of primary colours makes yellow?
quiz.why: In the RGB system, mixing red and green light beams creates the colour yellow.

wrong.1: Mixing red and blue light creates the colour magenta.
wrong.2: Mixing green and blue light creates the colour cyan.
wrong.3: Mixing all three creates white light, not just yellow.

quiz.say: If you use a very strong compression setting, what is the main risk?
quiz.show: Loss of detail due to compression

options.show: The file will become too big
options.say: The file will become too big

options.show: The colours will all turn black
options.say: The colours will all turn black

quiz.why: Compression works by removing data; removing too much data lowers the quality.

wrong.0: Compression's main goal is to make the file size smaller.
wrong.1: While colours can change, the whole image does not necessarily turn black.
wrong.2: The image data is usually kept, just less detailed.
